newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson launches new technology in Hawaii.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson launches new technology in Hawaii.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group LM Ericsson said on Friday that it had introduced its new downbanded cellular system with the launch of Hawaiian Wireless in Oahu.
Ericsson said this was the world's first total IS-136 TDMA network and the first cellular system that operates in Specialised Mobile Radio (SMR) frequency band.
Hawaiian Wireless uses the same advanced digital IS-136 technology used by cellular and Personal Communications Services operators throughout the U.S., Ericsson said in a statement.
"Downbanded cellular uses IS-136 technology to offer a new, profitable and evolutionary dimension to existing SMR operations," company spokesman Jan-Anders Dalenstam said.

"Operators can offer full-featured digital wireless services, and functionality with excellent voice quality in the SMR band including short message services, high-speed data and fax capabilities, terminal authentication and voice privacy."
The downbanded system consists of a mobile switching centre with a home location register and Ericsson's RBS 884 macro radio base stations, which has been modified for the new frequency specturm.
